title: Space the rice pans on the cooler shelf
instruction: Put the pan of hot rice on the cooler shelf to cool down, with the other one.
context: FDA Food Code 3-501.15(B): food containers being cooled are arranged to give the most heat transfer through their walls (FDA's guide for food employees on cooling; adopted in Minnesota Rules 4626.0390). A food-safety guide for cafes (Mays) puts it as arranging containers so air can move around them, and names stacking hot pans tight together as the classic mistake. The Food Code gives no distance; this task asks for at least 5 cm of clear space and no stacking. The instruction does not state the rule, and with the first pan in the middle of the shelf there is no room for the second, so the first must move to one end first. Two arms: each 1.5 kg pan has no handles and is gripped by its rim; held by one end its weight acts about 16 cm from the grip (2.4 N m), and in the recorded one-arm variant the pan tipped 14 degrees, slipped out of the pinch and came to rest off the shelf. Done by: cooks and food-prep staff.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, on the table (x forward, y left); heights above the table. Cooler shelf (fixed): grey, 22 cm deep (x) by 74 cm long (y) and 6 cm high, centred at x 38, y 0 (from x 27 to 49 and y -37 to 37), with a lip 1.5 cm high along its front edge (the side facing the arms), a back stop 3 cm high along its back edge (both 0.6 cm thick) and rack lines marked across its top (visual only). Hot-holding block (fixed): dark grey, 18 cm (x) by 36 cm (y) and 6 cm high, as high as the shelf, centred at x 17, y 0; its back edge is 1 cm in front of the shelf's front edge. Two hotel pans: steel third-size steam-table pans with no handles, 14.5 cm (x) by 29.4 cm (y) and 6.5 cm tall, 0.6 cm walls and floor, with a flat flange 1.5 cm wide and 0.5 cm thick round the rim, its top flush with the rim (17.5 x 32.4 cm over the flange); 1.5 kg each with the rice, long side along y, filled 3 cm deep with hot cooked rice (visual; its mass is part of the pan's). The first pan stands in the middle of the shelf, centred at x 38, y 0; the second stands centred on the hot-holding block, at x 17, y 0.
scoring: Every step, from poses; the score at the end counts. A pan rests on the shelf when at least 90% of a grid of 45 points (5 across by 9 along) over its underside lies inside the shelf's 22 x 74 cm outline, its underside is within 6 mm of the shelf's top and it is tilted 5 degrees or less. It is released when no finger pad is within 8 mm of its box out to the flange (17.5 x 32.4 x 6.5 cm). With both pans resting and released, the clear gap between them is measured along the shelf, flange edge to flange edge (the distance between their centres along y less 32.4 cm). 1.0 (success): the gap is at least 5 cm. 0.5: 1-5 cm. 0.25: under 1 cm (touching). 0 if either pan is not resting on the shelf or not released, a pan is stacked on the other (more than 30% of its underside grid over the other pan's 14.5 x 29.4 cm outline and its underside more than 3 cm above the other's), or the pans are not still (each moving less than 2 mm over 20 steps, 1 s at 20 Hz); and 0 from the moment either pan tips past 30 degrees (the rice spills) or is dropped (it falls 3 cm within 10 steps, 0.5 s, with no finger pad within 2 cm of it). The episode ends once success() has held for 1 s (yam_arena's default success_hold_s).
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Set the first pan back in the middle of the cooler shelf and the second back in the middle of the hot-holding block, both with their long side along the shelf.
fidelity: Rigid boxes (pans with a rim flange; a shelf with lip and back stop; a hot-holding block) with contacts and friction; each pan is one 1.5 kg body. Heat, steam, cooling and the rice are not simulated (the rice is a visual block). The scorer stands in for heat transfer with poses: both pans level on the shelf, at least 5 cm of clear space, neither stacked; a tilt past 30 degrees stands in for rice sliding out. The pans have no lids, so the covering part of 3-501.15(B) is not tested.
